questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's judgment of 11 March 2026 in Harish Rana v. Union of India, consider the following statements:
1. The Court treated clinically assisted nutrition and hydration through a PEG tube as medical treatment.
2. It was the first application of the passive-euthanasia framework laid down in Common Cause v. Union of India (2018).
3. The Court held that withdrawal of treatment can be permitted only after Parliament enacts an end-of-life care law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The bench of Justices Pardiwala and Viswanathan treated assisted nutrition as medical treatment and applied the 2018 Common Cause framework for the first time to a real patient. It only urged the Union to legislate; it did not make a statute a precondition, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.h: Common Cause 2018 was the blueprint; Harish Rana was the first real case.

questions.q: In Rachana Gangu v. Union of India (10 March 2026), the Supreme Court directed the Union Government to
o: declare vaccine manufacturers liable for deaths following Covid-19 vaccination under the Consumer Protection Act
dissolve the existing AEFI committees and replace them with a judicial commission
require families to pursue individual civil or consumer remedies for vaccine-related deaths
frame a no-fault compensation policy for serious adverse events or deaths following Covid-19 vaccination, without attributing any death to the vaccines
questions.e: The Court rejected the Centre's plea that families must go to civil or consumer forums and relied on Articles 21 and 14 to order a no-fault policy. It held existing AEFI committees adequate and made clear that compensation is not an admission that vaccines caused the deaths.
questions.h: No-fault means pay without blaming the vaccine.

questions.q: In Union of India v. Rohith Nathan (March 2026), the Supreme Court dealt with the creamy-layer exclusion among OBCs. Which one of the following best states its holding?
o: Salary income of the parents alone is the sole test of creamy-layer status
The creamy-layer status of a child is primarily status-based, depending on the category of the parent's post, and parental salary income alone cannot decide it
A 2004 DoPT clarificatory letter prevails over the 1993 Office Memorandum issued after Indra Sawhney
The creamy-layer exclusion does not apply to the children of government employees
questions.e: The bench of Justices Narasimha and Mahadevan held that the 2004 DoPT letter cannot override the 1993 OM issued after Indra Sawhney, and that salary income alone cannot settle creamy-layer status. It directed affected claims to be reconsidered within six months and allowed supernumerary posts.
questions.h: Post, not pay: the parent's post decides.

questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's judgment of 17 March 2026 in Hamsaanandini Nanduri v. Union of India, consider the following statements:
1. The Court struck down the age limit in Section 60(4) of the Code on Social Security, 2020.
2. The struck-down provision had limited the benefit to adoptive mothers of children below three months.
3. The Court held that an adoptive mother is entitled to 26 weeks of maternity leave.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Section 60(4) gave adoption leave only if the child was under three months; the Court held this violated Articles 14 and 21 and extended 12 weeks of leave to any woman legally adopting a child, whatever the child's age. The figure of 26 weeks is the leave for a biological mother's first two children, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.h: Adoption leave: 12 weeks, any age of child.

questions.q: Under Paragraph 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, as upheld by the Supreme Court in Chinthada Anand v. State of Andhra Pradesh (24 March 2026), persons professing which of the following religions can be treated as Scheduled Castes?
questions.e: Paragraph 3 originally recognised only Hindus; Sikhs were added in 1956 and Buddhists in 1990. The Court held that a person converting to any other religion loses Scheduled Caste status. Jainism is not in the list, which is the usual trap.
questions.h: 1950 Hindu, 1956 Sikh, 1990 Buddhist.

questions.q: In Prabhu Kumar v. State of Himachal Pradesh (2026), the Supreme Court invalidated a State's cap of 60 per cent disability for appointment as Assistant District Attorney. Which one of the following was the main reasoning?
o: Persons with disabilities cannot be reserved posts in prosecution services under any law
Article 15(4) bars States from prescribing any disability limits

The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 sets only a 40 per cent benchmark, and suitability must rest on the functional requirements of the post, so the arbitrary ceiling violated Articles 14 and 16
Disability benchmarks can be fixed only by the High Court of the State
questions.e: The Himachal Pradesh High Court had upheld the cap, but the Supreme Court said that a percentage bracket cannot replace an assessment of whether a person can perform the post's functions. A benchmark disability under the RPwD Act, 2016 is 40 per cent or more, so an upper ceiling of 60 per cent is arbitrary.
questions.h: 40 per cent is the floor; no arbitrary ceiling.

questions.q:
A nine-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court, led by CJI Surya Kant, reserved judgment on 19 March 2026 in a reference relating to Bangalore Water Supply v. A. Rajappa (1978). Consider the following statements:
1. The reference is about the correct definition of 'industry' under Section 2(j) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
2. The Rajappa 'triple test' gave 'industry' a wide meaning, covering many service and charitable establishments.
3. The reference concerns the definition of 'factory' under the Factories Act, 1948.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Rajappa (1978) defined 'industry' widely through its triple test, bringing hospitals, educational and charitable bodies within the Industrial Disputes Act, and the nine-judge bench has been asked whether that reading is correct. The reference has nothing to do with the Factories Act, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.h: Rajappa = how wide is 'industry'?

questions.q:
The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026 was passed by Parliament on 25 March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The Lok Sabha passed the Bill by voice vote the day before the Rajya Sabha approved it.
2. The Bill removes self-perceived gender identity and requires a District Magistrate to issue the certificate on a medical board's recommendation.
3. The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha by the Minister of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Lok Sabha passed it on 24 March amid an Opposition walkout, and the Rajya Sabha on 25 March. The 2019 Act allowed self-perceived identity, which the amendment replaces with a medical-board route; critics say this conflicts with the NALSA (2014) principle of self-identification. The Bill was introduced by Social Justice Minister Dr Virendra Kumar, not the Home Minister.
questions.h: Self-ID out, medical board in.

questions.q: The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 25 March 2026. What does it provide when an FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered or ceases?
o: Foreign contributions and assets created from them vest provisionally in a Designated Authority, and permanently if no fresh or renewed registration is obtained within the prescribed period
They are returned to the foreign donor within thirty days
They vest immediately and permanently in the Consolidated Fund of India
They remain with the association until a court orders otherwise
questions.e: The Bill creates a Designated Authority to take provisional custody of foreign funds and assets bought from them once registration ends, and the vesting becomes permanent if the association fails to obtain a new registration in time. FCRA, 2010 is administered by the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Bill was still pending when the Budget Session ended.
questions.h: Registration ends, assets go to a Designated Authority.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Jan Vishwas legislation in March 2026:
1. The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2025 was withdrawn from the Lok Sabha on 17 March 2026 after the Select Committee presented its report.
2. The replacement Bill of 2026 amends 80 central Acts, whereas the 2025 Bill had amended 80 Acts as well.
3. The Select Committee was chaired by the Minister of Law and Justice.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2025 Bill was withdrawn after the Select Committee (chaired by Tejasvi Surya, not the Law Minister) reported on 13 March. The 2026 Bill replaced it and amends 80 Acts, but the 2025 Bill had amended only 17 Acts, so statements 2 and 3 are wrong.
questions.h: From 17 Acts to 80: withdraw and replace.

questions.q:
The Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Bill, 2026, passed by both Houses of the State Legislature, seeks to prohibit unlawful conversion. Consider the following statements:
1. A person intending to convert must give the District Magistrate a declaration at least 60 days in advance.
2. Relatives by blood, marriage or adoption can file a complaint even if an adult converts voluntarily.
3. Voluntary conversions are exempt from all notice requirements.
4. The general punishment is a fine only, with no imprisonment.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 60-day declaration to the District Magistrate, a post-conversion declaration and prior notice from the facilitating priest apply even to voluntary conversions, so statement 3 is wrong. Complaints can come from the converted person, parents, siblings and relatives by blood, marriage or adoption. The general penalty is imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine up to Rs 1 lakh, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.h: Notice applies even to voluntary converts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Bill, 2026, passed by Parliament:
1. It applies to the CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP and SSB listed in its First Schedule.
2. Assam Rifles and the NSG are included in the First Schedule at present.
3. All posts in the ranks of Director General and Special Director General must be filled by deputation of IPS officers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Bill is an overarching law for recruitment, deputation, promotion and service conditions of officers in the five major CAPFs. Assam Rifles and the NSG are not covered at present, though the Centre may amend the Schedule. IPS deputation covers 50 per cent of IG posts, at least 67 per cent of ADG posts and all DG and Special DG posts.
questions.h: Five forces; Assam Rifles and NSG left out.

questions.q:
The Opposition moved a no-confidence notice against Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla. Consider the following statements on the removal of the Speaker:
1. The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House.
2. A resolution for removal cannot be moved unless at least 14 days' notice has been given.
3. A simple majority of members present and voting is enough to remove the Speaker.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 94(c) needs an effective majority, a majority of the total membership rather than of those present and voting, so statement 3 is wrong. The proviso demands 14 days' notice, and leave to move the resolution needs the support of at least 50 members. Earlier motions against Mavalankar (1954), Hukam Singh (1966) and Balram Jakhar (1987) all failed.
questions.h: Think whole House, not those present.

questions.q: The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 23 March 2026. To which body was it referred?
o: A Select Committee of the Lok Sabha
The Rajya Sabha Committee on Subordinate Legislation
questions.e: Unlike the Jan Vishwas Bill, which went to a Select Committee, the Corporate Laws Bill was sent to a Joint Parliamentary Committee drawn from both Houses. Of the 13 Bills introduced in the Budget Session 2026, nine were passed, one was withdrawn and one (the 131st Constitution Amendment Bill on delimitation) was later voted down.
questions.h: Corporate Laws goes to a joint panel.

questions.q: In the biennial Rajya Sabha elections held on 16 March 2026 for 37 seats across 10 States, polling had to be held for 11 seats because the candidates were not elected unopposed. In which of the following States was polling held?
questions.e: Twenty-six candidates were elected unopposed and polling was held for five seats in Bihar, four in Odisha and two in Haryana. Rajya Sabha members are elected by the elected members of State legislatures through single transferable vote, and the House has 245 members, of whom 233 are elected and 12 nominated by the President.
questions.h: Contest in Bihar (5), Odisha (4), Haryana (2).

questions.q:
The Election Commission announced assembly elections on 15 March 2026. Consider the following pairs:
State/UT : Polling date
1. Assam : 9 April 2026
2. Puducherry : 23 April 2026
3. Tamil Nadu : 23 April 2026
4. West Bengal : 23 and 29 April 2026 (two phases)
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Assam, Kerala and Puducherry vote on 9 April, Tamil Nadu on 23 April and West Bengal in two phases on 23 and 29 April, with counting on 4 May. Puducherry is therefore wrongly matched with 23 April. About 17.4 crore electors are eligible across 824 constituencies, and the Model Code of Conduct applied from the announcement.
questions.h: Three go early; Tamil Nadu 23 April; Bengal two phases.

questions.q:
On 5 March 2026 the President reshuffled nine Governors and Lieutenant Governors. Consider the following statements:
1. R.N. Ravi was moved from Tamil Nadu to West Bengal.
2. Former diplomat Taranjit Singh Sandhu was appointed Lieutenant Governor of Delhi.
3. V.K. Saxena was moved to Ladakh as Lieutenant Governor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three appointments formed part of the 5 March reshuffle. Kerala's Governor Rajendra Arlekar was also given additional charge of Tamil Nadu, and C.V. Ananda Bose's resignation as West Bengal Governor was accepted. Governors are appointed under Article 155, and Delhi's Lieutenant Governor has special powers under Article 239AA.
questions.h: Ravi to Bengal, Sandhu to Delhi, Saxena to Ladakh.

questions.q:
The Garo Hills Autonomous District Council polls in Meghalaya, set for 10 April 2026, were postponed. Consider the following statements:
1. The postponement followed unrest over a notification requiring candidates to hold a Scheduled Tribe certificate.
2. Meghalaya has three Autonomous District Councils: Garo Hills, Khasi Hills and Jaintia Hills.
3. Autonomous District Councils are created under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Plains non-tribals objected to the ST-certificate requirement and argued that only Parliament can amend the Sixth Schedule; the polls were put off and the Council's term extended by six months. Autonomous District Councils exist under the Sixth Schedule for tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, while the Fifth Schedule governs Scheduled Areas in other States.
questions.h: Sixth Schedule means Autonomous District Councils.

questions.q:
The Election Commission extended the postal ballot facility to electors above 85 years of age and Persons with Disabilities. Consider the following statements:
1. Postal ballot voting is governed by the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961 and the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
2. Service voters include members of the armed forces and government servants posted abroad.
3. Persons under preventive detention are barred from voting by postal ballot.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Persons under preventive detention are among those who can vote by post, so statement 3 is wrong. The eligible groups are service voters, special voters, absentee voters such as seniors above 85 and PwDs, those under preventive detention, and election duty personnel. The framework sits in the 1961 Rules and the 1951 Act.
questions.h: Detained voters can vote by post.

questions.q: On 10 March 2026 the Supreme Court gave directions on electoral roll deletions in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in West Bengal. Which one of the following was directed?
o: Automatic restoration of all deleted names to the electoral roll without verification
Cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision and a return to the earlier rolls
Creation of an appellate mechanism for persons whose names were deleted, with the parties later asked to approach the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court to supervise it
Transfer of all appeals to the Election Commission of India for final decision
questions.e: The Court ordered an appellate route for those struck off the rolls and, on 24 March, asked the parties to approach the Calcutta High Court's Chief Justice to oversee the process. It did not scrap the revision, which the Election Commission ran ahead of the 2026 assembly election.
questions.h: Deleted names get an appeal route.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Parliamentary Standing Committee) with List-II (subject of its March 2026 report):
List-I
A. Empowerment of Women
B. Communications and IT
C. Agriculture
D. Health and Family Welfare
List-II
1. Replacing the Seeds Act, 1966 and expanding PM-AASHA procurement
2. Artificial Intelligence (Report No. 27)
3. All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi
4. Cyber crimes and cyber safety of women
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The women's committee under Dr D. Purandeswari reported on cyber safety (23 March); the Communications and IT committee under Dr Nishikant Dubey reported on AI (30 March); the Agriculture committee under Charanjit Singh Channi on procurement and seeds (27 March); and the Health committee under Prof. Ram Gopal Yadav on AIIMS Delhi (18 March, 171st report).
questions.h: Women-cyber, IT-AI, Agriculture-seeds, Health-AIIMS.

questions.q:
The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and IT presented its Report No. 27 on Artificial Intelligence on 30 March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It recommended that the Government explore comprehensive AI legislation.
2. It recommended age restrictions on certain platforms.
3. It recommended that AI education be kept out of schools and colleges until a law is enacted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The committee, chaired by Dr Nishikant Dubey, called for the Government to look at comprehensive AI legislation and age limits on certain platforms. It also urged AI education in schools and colleges and faster amendments to the IT Rules, which is the opposite of statement 3.
questions.h: Law and age limits yes, AI education also yes.

questions.q:
Speaker Om Birla nominated 15 members to the Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges, to be chaired by Ravi Shankar Prasad. Consider the following statements:
1. The Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges has 15 members, while the Rajya Sabha committee has 10.
2. Parliamentary privileges are provided for in Articles 105 and 194 of the Constitution for Parliament and State Legislatures respectively.
3. Parliament has enacted a comprehensive law that codifies all privileges of its members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: No law passed by Parliament codifies privileges; they rest on the Constitution, the Rules of Procedure and conventions, so statement 3 is wrong. Articles 105 and 122 cover Parliament, while 194 and 212 cover State Legislatures. The committee examines breaches of privilege and recommends action, a semi-judicial role.
questions.h: No statute codifies privileges.

questions.q:
The Ministry of Home Affairs revised the Look Out Circular (LOC) guidelines in March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. Statutory bodies such as the NCW, NHRC, NCPCR and NCLT can no longer directly ask the Bureau of Immigration to open an LOC.
2. Such requests must now be routed through a law-enforcement agency with criminal jurisdiction.
3. The 'see remarks' action in the LOC proforma is reserved for intelligence agencies in counter-terrorism cases.
4. The Bureau of Immigration functions under the Ministry of External Affairs.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The new rules close the direct route for statutory commissions and tribunals; they must go through a law-enforcement agency. The proforma now has three actions (detain and inform, prevent departure and inform, see remarks), with 'see remarks' restricted to intelligence agencies. The Bureau of Immigration works under the Ministry of Home Affairs, not External Affairs.
questions.h: LOC requests must come through police-type agencies.

questions.q: The Union Cabinet on 25 March 2026 approved the continuation of the Immigration, Visa, Foreigners Registration and Tracking (IVFRT) Scheme from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031, with an outlay of Rs 1,800 crore. Which one of the following correctly describes the scheme?
o: It is run by the Ministry of External Affairs and aligned with the Passports Act, 1967
It is run by the Ministry of Home Affairs and aligned with the Foreigners Act, 1946
It is run by the Ministry of Civil Aviation and aligned with the Citizenship Act, 1955
It is run by the Ministry of Home Affairs and aligned with the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025
questions.e: IVFRT is a Home Ministry scheme first approved in 2010. Version 3.0 aligns with the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, which replaced older laws such as the Foreigners Act, 1946. It adds iris scanning, AI and ML tools and self-service kiosks at immigration check posts.
questions.h: Home Ministry, new 2025 law.
